topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Biology and Lecture Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, framing the clinical significance of cancer and outlining the session's core learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic Basis and Cellular Differentiation in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancers arise through stepwise genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal tissue architecture and developmental differentiation programs.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the pathological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors by detailing the processes of basement membrane invasion, metastatic dissemination, and adenoma-to-carcinoma progression.

topics.label: Neoplasm Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the systematic naming conventions and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors across various tissue lineages.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Morbidity and Mortality in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the anatomical, metabolic, and metastatic mechanisms through which tumors compromise organ function and cause patient death.

topics.label: Comparative Tumor Incidence Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of cancer incidence and tissue susceptibility in humans alongside comparative findings across companion animals and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Cancer Screening Principles and Clinical Applications
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the rationale, diagnostic techniques, and relative success rates of population-level screening programs across different anatomical sites.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and pointing forward to upcoming practicals and lectures.
